person.occupation: member of the Corporation of London for the Ward of Cheap

note.p: The Times, reports his death on 20 November 1818, 'Alderman Goodbehere had been for nearly thirty years a distinguished member of the Corporation of London', where he was an ally of the radical Robert Waithman. The Morning Chronicle, 28 November 1818, lists Waithman and Alderman Wood amongst those at his funeral. Godwin records his death. The identification is confirmed by 17 January 1815: 'Court of Aldermen; adv. Goodbehere, Reeves, Thos Bell and Line'.

Ed Pope adds: 27.11.1795 Goodbehe at Crown and Anchor, This dinner at the Crown and Anchor wasn't advertised in the newspapers and seems to have been only attended by 15 or so people as Godwin lists names followed by "and 2" changed to 3 (or "and 3" changed to 2), but though it could be an anniversary celebration of the acquittals in the treason trials, Bonney and Tooke being present, it was more likely to be discussing the sedition bills, the hot topic of the day. The Crown and Anchor in the Strand was happy to host political associations of all stripes Goodbehere had been a common councilman for Cheap Ward since 1786 and on 9.6.1796 he was one of the stewards at a dinner celebrating the election to Parliament of Alderman Combe, who had led the opposition to the sedition bills in Common Hall in November 1795.
